{{Quote|Ajunta Pall beheaded their ruler, Hakagram Graush, and claimed the throne as the blood heir to the ancestral King Adas&mdash;and we became his Shadow Hands.|Sorzus Syn|<ref name="BOS" />}}
'''Hakagram Graush''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] of the [[Sith Empire (Pre-Republic)|Sith Empire]] who ruled on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] as the [[Sith King]] around the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[6900 BBY]]. After the [[Discovery of Korriban|arrival]] of the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[exiles]] on Korriban, following the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]], the [[Sith sorcerer]] and monarch, alongside his people, disallowed the outsiders from learning their secrets of [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]]. However, through the monarch's [[Hakagram Graush's Shadow Hand|second-in-command]] known as the [[Shadow Hand]], the numerous Dark [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] eventually lured the King into their confidence. [[Ajunta Pall]], the leader of the Dark Jedi, [[Death/Legends|beheaded]] Graush with the King's own [[Sith war sword|war sword]].

With Graush's [[Death/Legends|death]], Pall usurped the King's throne, and the Dark Jedi became [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] themselves, taking Graush's position over the Sith people he once ruled. The deceased King was buried inside a [[Tomb of Hakagram Graush|tomb]] in the [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Sleeping Kings]]. Thousands of years after the King's demise, the tomb received a visit from the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]], who was inquiring on the existence of [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghosts]], but no specter of Graush ever showed itself.

==Biography==
===Life as a Monarch===
{{Quote|The Sith greeted us. Despite our obvious superior powers, we were not hailed as gods when we arrived.|Sorzus Syn|<ref name="BOS" />}}
[[File:Moraband-FDCR.png|thumb|left|250px|Korriban, Graush's barren and cold homeworld]]
Hakagram Graush was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] member of the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]],<ref name="END:TSD" /> a species of [[Blood/Legends|blood]]-[[Color/Legends|colored]], violent [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]]<ref name="JvS:TEGttF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> originating from [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], a barren [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located within the [[Stygian Caldera]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Like most members of his [[Species/Legends|species]], Graush was strongly [[Force-sensitive/Legends|connected]] with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]],<ref name="dbsith">{{DB|organization|thesith|Sith}}</ref> and he shared his surname with famed [[Sith sorcerer]] [[Dathka Graush/Legends|Dathka Graush]]<ref name="BOS" /> and the [[Graush dynasty]].<ref name="wizards2">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031016korriban3|series=Korriban: Planet of Lost Souls|text=Part 3: The Dark Lord's Heart}}</ref>

Eventually, Graush was [[Crown/Legends|crowned]] [[Sith King|king]] of his people. The monarch ruled over the [[Sith Empire (Pre-Republic)|Sith Empire]] with the help of the [[Shadow Hand]], his [[Hakagram Graush's Shadow Hand|second-in-command]].<ref name="END:TSD" /> During his reign, Graush built a [[Hakagram Graush's palace|palace]] on [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]], the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of the ancient [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="BOS" /> His reign lasted until around [[6900 BBY]],<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> with the [[Discovery of Korriban|arrival]] of the [[Exiles]], a group of [[Dark Jedi/Legends|fallen]] [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who had been [[Battle of Corbos|defeated]] in a [[The galaxy/Legends|pan-galactic]] war called the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]].<ref name="END:TSD" /> The Exiles' leader, High General [[Ajunta Pall]],<ref name="BOS" /> took particular interest in the techniques that the Sith used for drawing power from the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]].<ref name="TOJC">''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]''</ref> Despite the strangers' greater [[Force power/Legends|powers]] and superior weapons called [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]], Graush and his Sith did not immediately hail them as [[Deity/Legends|deities]] when they arrived.<ref name="BOS" />

===Downfall of the King===
{{Quote|It took weeks for us to understand the power structure of their culture, to undermine it, and to annihilate the current king.|Sorzus Syn|<ref name="BOS" />}}
Unbeknownst to Graush, the Dark Jedi infiltrated the power structure of the Sith society, seeking to undermine the monarch's authority from within.<ref name="BOS" /> Betrayed by his own Shadow Hand,<ref name="END:TSD" /> Graush was lured into the Exiles' confidence, which led him to his [[Death/Legends|death]] as Pall eventually decided to execute the Sith King. Graush was literally brought on his knees and [[Sai cha/Legends|beheaded]] by a swipe of his own [[Sith war sword|war sword]]. The [[Kissai]] believed that Pall was a manifestation of [[Typhojem/Legends|Typhojem]] and coronated him as their [[Jen'ari]], or [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]].<ref name="BOS" />

Pall rose to power over the people of Korriban and Ziost, appointing himself as the rightful heir of the famed King [[Adas]]. Pall and his cohorts, including the [[Human/Legends|Human]] female [[Sorzus Syn]], eventually pronounced themselves [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]]. Even though he had been stripped of his throne and murdered, Graush was buried with due honors in the [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Sleeping Kings]], Korriban's majestic [[Burial/Legends|burial]] grounds.<ref name="BOS" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|The tomb of Hakagram Graush remained silent to my queries.|Darth Plagueis|<ref name="BOS" />}}
[[File:Plagueis_head.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Darth Plagueis sought to contact the spirit of Graush.]]
With Graush's demise, the [[Sith/Legends|Sith Order]] was founded, and the culture of the Sith species was turned into a dark side religion.<ref name="TOJC" /> However, [[Standard year/Legends|millennia]] after his death, the name of Hakagram Graush was still remembered. The [[Muun/Legends|Muun]] [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] traveled to Korriban and visited the burial grounds, then renamed the Valley of the Dark Lords, in hopes of encountering Sith [[Force ghost/Legends|spirits]] and query them for their long-lost secrets.<ref name="BOS" />

Among other symbolic locations such as the [[Sorzus Syn's throne|throne of Sorzus Syn]], Plagueis entered the [[Tomb of Hakagram Graush|tomb of Graush]] and tried to contact the specter of the last Sith King, to no avail. Plagueis witnessed no manifestation of a ghost, which reinforced his belief that there was no such thing. Plagueis wrote a succinct note about this lack of supernatural incident in his [[Book of Sith|scientific journal]].<ref name="BOS" />

==Personality and traits==
A crimson-skinned Sith, Hakagram Graush was tall and muscular. Unlike most other Sith, he had five [[Limb/Legends|fingers]] per hand instead of the usual three.<ref name="GAotS:Funeral" /> When he chose to appear bare-headed, the King's long dark [[Hair/Legends|hair]] could be seen flowing on his neck. When Graush first met the Exiles, he was not overly impressed by the newcomers' superior technology. He did not hail them as deities, considering the Exiles powerful but not godlike.<ref name="BOS" />

==Equipment==
In spite of Korriban's cold climate,<ref name="wizards1">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031002korriban1|series=Korriban: Planet of Lost Souls|text=Part 1: Haunted Hideout}}</ref> he used to go [[Breast/Legends|barechested]], wearing only a [[Cape/Legends|cape]] and an elaborate [[loincloth]]. Like most of his peers at the [[Time/Legends|time]], he wore many types of ornaments, including metal bracers and shin [[Armor/Legends|armors]]. Graush also wore a helmet made of the [[Bone/Legends|skull]] of a horned creature, with a neck guard made from small metal scales.<ref name="GAotS:Funeral" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I'd originally written the king's identity as Dathka Graush, but upon researching the timeline a bit more it became obvious that Dathka wouldn't work. Instead I introduced Hakagram Graush as his presumed descendent ''[sic]''.|Daniel Wallace|<ref name="BOS endnotes">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2012/03/endnotes-for-star-wars-book-of-sith.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: Book of Sith (part 1)|date=2012-03-09}}</ref>}}
[[File:Graush_beheaded.png|thumb|left|250px|In ''Book of Sith'', Graush was mistakenly depicted as being killed by Pall with a lightsaber.]]
Hakagram Graush, last King of the Sith, first appeared in the [[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2|second issue]] of the [[1996]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series ''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith]]''.<ref name="GAotS:Funeral" /> The monarch went unnamed in the series, and his identity was only revealed in [[2012]], with the publication of ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''.<ref name="BOS" /> [[Daniel Wallace]], author of the ''Book of Sith'', originally intended the murdered monarch to be the Sith sorcerer Dathka Graush. However, Wallace realized it would not fit with Dathka's established timeline, and he introduced his probable descendant Hakagram instead.<ref name="BOS endnotes" />

While the text in ''Book of Sith'' clearly states that Ajunta Pall beheaded Hakagram Graush using the monarch's own [[Sword/Legends|sword]], a picture depicts Pall using a lightsaber. In his endnotes, Wallace admitted he did not catch that mistake when he reviewed the artwork.<ref name="BOS endnotes" />

In the [[Knights of the Old Republic 29|twenty-ninth issue]] of the [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic (comic series)|''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic'']] series of comics, a horned helmet known as the [[Helm of Dathka Graush]] was shown.<ref name="KOR29">[[Knights of the Old Republic 29|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 29]]</ref> The design of this helmet is similar to the one Hakagram Graush wore in ''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 2.<ref name="GAotS:Funeral" />

In [[Tales of the Jedi Companion]], [[Ood Bnar]] says that the Sith "were not united, preferring to remain in tribal 'circles,'" when Ajunta Pall conquered them, but Ood Bnar lived in [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]],<ref name="TOJC" /> 2900 years after Ajunta Pall,<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> while Sorzus Syn witnessed Ajunta Pall meeting and beheading Graush<ref name="BOS" />, so this article assumes that Bnar was misinformed.
